slides.title: ADHD mom + messy kids: tiny systems that don't need nagging
One bin per toy type, with a picture
slides.body: Kids can't read labels, and honestly neither can we when tired. Tape a photo of what goes in each bin.

slides.title: No lids on kid bins
slides.body: Lids add a step. One step too many, and toys stay on the floor. Open bins, low shelves.

slides.title: The 5-minute tidy song
slides.body: Same song every night, everyone tidies until it ends. The song is the timer and the signal.

slides.title: A hook for everything at kid height
slides.body: Backpack, coat, and bag hooks they can reach. If they need you to hang it, it hits the floor.

slides.title: Toy rotation
slides.body: Put half the toys in a closet. Swap monthly. Less to clean, and old toys feel new again.

slides.title: If a 4-year-old can't put it away, the system is too complicated. For me too.
Systems for the whole family
slides.body: The Messy Brain Home Reset includes a kid-friendly 7-day reset you can do together. Link in bio.
